results.question: A zoning lot assembled in 2026 straddles two zoning districts, with more than 50 percent of its area in the less restrictive district. Can that majority district's use regulations automatically apply to the entire zoning lot under Section 77-11?

answer.answerText:
**No.** Having more than 50 percent of the area in the less restrictive district does not automatically extend that district’s use regulations to the entire zoning lot. Under ZR § 77-11, that district’s regulations *may* apply only if the zoning lot existed on December 15, 1961, or the applicable subsequent amendment date, and the greatest perpendicular distance from the mapped district boundary to any lot line in the minority portion is no more than 25 feet. If those conditions are met, the district boundary may be assumed relocated and the expanded district’s bulk, parking, loading, and other regulations apply to the entire lot. A special-purpose-district provision can independently limit or govern application of § 77-11. (ZR § 77-11)

For a lot assembled in 2026, the applicable existence or amendment-date condition is unresolved; the 2026 assembly date alone does not identify the controlling amendment date or establish eligibility under § 77-11. If the lot did not exist on the applicable date, ZR § 77-02 instead provides that each portion is regulated by the district in which it is located, subject to its separate Floor Area Ratio rule in § 77-22. (ZR § 77-02; ZR § 77-22)
answer.conclusion: **No.** Having more than 50 percent of the area in the less restrictive district does not automatically extend that district’s use regulations to the entire zoning lot. Under ZR § 77-11, that district’s regulations *may* apply only if the zoning lot existed on December 15, 1961, or the applicable subsequent amendment date, and the greatest perpendicular distance from the mapped district boundary to any lot line in the minority portion is no more than 25 feet. If those conditions are met, the district boundary may be assumed relocated and the expanded district’s bulk, parking, loading, and other regulations apply to the entire lot. A special-purpose-district provision can independently limit or govern application of § 77-11. (ZR § 77-11)

supportedPoints.heading: Majority-area rule is conditional, not automatic
supportedPoints.explanation: ZR § 77-11 provides that the use regulations of the district containing more than 50 percent of the zoning-lot area may apply to the entire zoning lot only when the lot existed on December 15, 1961, or on the applicable subsequent amendment date, and the greatest distance from the mapped district boundary to any lot line in the minority portion does not exceed 25 feet, measured perpendicular to that boundary. If the use regulations are so applied, the boundary may be assumed relocated and the expanded district’s bulk, off-street parking and loading, and other regulations apply to the entire zoning lot. The section also preserves special-purpose-district provisions as a potential governing limitation or condition.

supportedPoints.heading: Later-created lots are generally regulated portion by portion
supportedPoints.explanation: ZR § 77-02 states that when a zoning lot did not exist on December 15, 1961, or on an applicable subsequent amendment date, each portion is regulated by the provisions applicable to the district in which that portion is located. A 2026 assembly date alone does not establish which effective or amendment date applies or conclusively resolve that predicate.

supportedPoints.heading: FAR is treated separately
supportedPoints.explanation: ZR § 77-02 expressly provides that ZR § 77-22 applies to zoning lots created at any time where different bulk regulations apply to different portions. Section 77-22 calculates an adjusted maximum FAR by multiplying each applicable portion’s FAR by that portion’s percentage of the zoning lot and summing the products; the resulting floor area may be located anywhere on the zoning lot subject to the stated limitations.

supportingPassages.selectedText: Whenever a zoning lot existing on December 15, 1961, or on any applicable subsequent amendment thereto, is divided by a boundary between districts in which different uses are permitted, the use regulations applicable to the district in which more than 50 percent of the lot area of the zoning lot is located may apply to the entire zoning lot, provided that the greatest distance from the mapped district boundary to any lot line of such zoning lot in the district in which less than 50 percent of its area is located does not exceed 25 feet. Such distance shall be measured perpendicular to the mapped district boundary. Whenever the use regulations are so applied, the district boundary may be assumed to be relocated accordingly, and the bulk, off-street parking and loading, and all other regulations applying to such expanded district shall apply to the entire zoning lot. However, when the zoning lot is divided by a district boundary between a district limited to single- or two-family residences and a district permitting multiple dwellings, the use and bulk regulations of an R3-2 District shall apply in the R1, R2, R3A, R3X or R3-1 portion, and the use and bulk regulations of an R4 District shall apply in the R2X, R4A, R4-1 or R4B portion. Except as specifically provided by the provisions of a special purpose district, the provisions of this Section shall apply to zoning lots which are divided by a special purpose district boundary line.

citations.relevance: Controls the conditional application of the majority district’s use regulations to the entire zoning lot, including the existence-date and 25-foot distance conditions and special-purpose-district qualification.

However, the provisions of Section 77-22 (Floor Area Ratio) shall apply to zoning lots created at any time where different bulk regulations apply to different portions of such zoning lot.

citations.relevance: Establishes the portion-by-portion rule for zoning lots not existing on the applicable effective or amendment date.

citations.title: Floor Area Ratio

supportingPassages.selectedText: The maximum floor area ratio permitted on each portion of such zoning lot for the applicable type of building or buildings on such zoning lot shall be determined under the applicable regulations of this Resolution. Each such floor area ratio shall be multiplied by the percentage of the zoning lot to which such floor area ratio applies. The sum of the products thus obtained shall be the adjusted maximum floor area ratio applicable to such zoning lot. The floor area resulting from application of the adjusted maximum floor area ratio may be located anywhere on the zoning lot, subject to all other regulations of this Resolution, and provided that the floor area ratio for any portion of the zoning lot within one district shall not exceed the maximum floor area ratio, specified for that district, or the adjusted maximum floor area ratio for the zoning lot, whichever is greater, except that the portion of the zoning lot fronting on and within 100 feet of a wide street and permitting the greater maximum permitted residential floor area ratio may exceed the maximum permitted residential floor area ratio for the portion of the zoning lot by up to 20 percent. In applying the provisions of this Section, the following conditions shall apply: the floor area bonus permitted for publicly accessible open areas or arcades, under the applicable regulations of this Resolution, shall apply only to such publicly accessible open areas, arcades or portions thereof, as are located in a district in which such bonus is granted; and when a zoning lot contains a sky exposure plane building which does not have a specified maximum floor area ratio, for the purpose of computing the adjusted maximum floor area ratio, the floor area ratio of such zoning lot shall be deemed to be that which can be achieved at the minimum required open space ratio for such zoning lot.

citations.relevance: Establishes the separate FAR treatment for zoning lots with different bulk regulations across portions.
